articles.title: A Texas homeowner wins $100,000 in attorney's fees after an appeals court upholds her award in a years-long HOA dispute over a backyard home office
articles.summary: Masha Davis, a homeowner in the Davis Spring Subdivision in Williamson County, Texas, has been awarded $100,000 in attorney's fees after a dispute with
articles.body: Masha Davis, a homeowner in the Davis Spring Subdivision in Williamson County, Texas, has been awarded $100,000 in attorney's fees after a dispute with her property owners' association over a backyard structure she described as a "home office". The association refused her 2020 application, citing a height restriction. A district court later declared that no restrictive covenant barred construction. On 29 September 2026, the Texas Court of Appeals, Third District, affirmed the fee award, finding the association had not preserved one argument and had inadequately briefed another.Why did the Texas HOA reject the homeowner's backyard officeThe opinion records that Davis then sued the Association for, among other things, violating the Declaration. According to the court, she argued that neither the Declaration nor the Design Guidelines contained a height restriction on accessory structures, so the ARC had no authority to deny her application. Her claims included breach of fiduciary duty for 'arbitrarily and capriciously enforcing the restrictive covenants', violations of the Federal and Texas Fair Housing Acts, and multiple claims for declaratory relief. The Association and its Board President, Amanda Mock, were the appellants in the later appeal.The Court of Appeals reports that the 395th District Court of Williamson County, presided over by Judge Ryan D. Larson, granted Davis partial summary judgment on some of her declaratory claims. The declarations included that the 2002 Design Guidelines were the only guidelines filed of record at the time, that they contained no height restriction prohibiting her structure, and that the ARC's denial 'did not provide any basis found in the 2002 Design Guidelines'. The district court also dismissed Davis's breach of fiduciary duty claims against the Association and Mock, and her Fair Housing Act claims against the Association. On a later motion, it declared that 'there are no restrictive covenants prohibiting Plaintiff from constructing her accessory structure as submitted'. The opinion adds that the court awarded Davis her reasonable and necessary attorney's fees under Section 5.006 of the Texas Property Code, and that the Association did not address her entitlement to those fees in its response to that motion.How much did the Texas homeowner demand in attorney's feesThe opinion states that Davis later obtained a partial nonsuit without prejudice on her remaining claims, and the case moved to a hearing on attorney's fees. According to the court, Davis's lawyer, a partner whose practice has focused since 2008 on civil litigation and real estate and HOA litigation, testified and produced detailed billing records. He told the court his firm charged $450 an hour for partners and $225 an hour for legal assistants, rates he described as prevailing in Williamson County, Travis County and surrounding counties. He testified that attorneys spent approximately 300 hours and legal assistants approximately 37 hours on the case, covering a period of 'over four years' from August 2020 to the date of his affidavit.The court records that counsel requested a total of $149,680.25, plus contingent appellate fees. Those were itemised in the opinion as $3,500 for a motion for new trial, $35,000 to respond to an appeal to the Third Court of Appeals, $15,000 to respond to a petition for review to the Texas Supreme Court, and $45,000 for further briefing if that court granted review. The opinion says the Association presented no evidence controverting Davis's evidence and argued only that she had failed to segregate her fees. The district court awarded $100,000, which the Court of Appeals describes as approximately $50,000 less than the amount requested, together with the contingent appellate fees in the amounts Davis had requested.Why did the Texas HOA challenge the $100,000 attorney's fee awardThe Association raised two issues on appeal. First, it argued that Davis was not entitled to fees under Section 5.006, which states: 'In an action based on breach of a restrictive covenant about real property, the court shall allow to a prevailing party who asserted the action reasonable attorney's fees in addition to the party's costs and claim.' According to the Court of Appeals, the Association had not raised this argument in the district court, either in response to the summary judgment motion, at the fees hearing, or in a motion for new trial. The court concluded the issue was not preserved for review and overruled it, citing Texas Rule of Appellate Procedure 33.1(a)(1).Second, the Association argued that Davis had failed to segregate her fees. The opinion states that the Association had 'inadequately briefed this issue' and that, in any case, the record supported the award. The court noted that Davis's counsel testified he had tried to segregate the fees but was unable to, because the work on the covenant enforcement, Fair Housing Act, fiduciary duty and declaratory claims was 'inextricably intertwined', and that work not based on the restrictive-covenant issue was 'at most, 5 to 10 per cent '. Applying what it called a 'relaxed standard' for segregation evidence, the court held that this testimony was sufficient to support the $100,000 award, which it described as 'approximately $50,000 and 33% less than the amount that Davis had requested'. Because the Association had not requested findings of fact and conclusions of law, the court said it must imply the findings needed to support the judgment. Justice Gisela D. Triana, writing for a panel that also included Justices Theofanis and Crump, concluded that it could not find an abuse of discretion and affirmed.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available information, including the memorandum opinion of the Texas Court of Appeals, Third District, in Case No. 03-24-00592-CV. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the dispute, the fee amounts or the circumstances mentioned. The information should not be interpreted as confirmation from Masha Davis, the Davis Spring Property Owners' Association, Inc., Amanda Mock or their representatives.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Minnesota couple found an 85-year-old widower's wedding ring inside a used car they had bought, then tracked him down at a concert after discovering he had worn it since 1962
articles.summary: A lost wedding ring returned to an 85-year-old widower in Bemidji, Minnesota, after a used-car sale sent it to strangers who refused to keep it.
articles.body: A lost wedding ring returned to an 85-year-old widower in Bemidji, Minnesota, after a used-car sale sent it to strangers who refused to keep it. Roger Reese had searched his Ford Escape repeatedly without success, then later sold the vehicle. The couple who bought it as a birthday present found the gold band tucked inside a door compartment and set out to trace its owner. Their search ended on 3 November, when Fred Ambuehl approached a volunteer arranging chairs for a country music concert, and the two men involved, both Vietnam veterans in their eighties, met for the first time.85-year-old Minnesota widower lost the wedding ring he had worn since 1962 during a driveAccording to The Washington Post, Reese lost the ring while driving in Bemidji. He had worn it since marrying his wife, Joan, in 1962, and it remained one of his most treasured possessions after her death. When he noticed it was missing, he searched the vehicle in case it had fallen somewhere inside, but found nothing. He eventually visited a pawnshop and bought a similar ring, though not the same one.Later, he moved into a senior living community. He no longer needed the Ford Escape and sold it, unaware that the original ring was still inside.Vickie Ambuehl noticed a gold ring in a door compartment while cleaning the Ford EscapeFred and Vickie Ambuehl wanted to clean the vehicle properly before using it. While doing so, Vickie spotted a gold wedding ring in one of the door compartments. The couple understood that nobody casually abandons a wedding ring, and that somewhere an owner was probably wondering whether he would ever see it again. Fred examined the band, and they began trying to learn who had owned the car before them.Paperwork bearing Reese's name sent a country music couple asking around senior living venuesPaperwork left inside the vehicle carried the name Roger Reese, but a name alone was not enough to find him. The Ambuehls still needed to work out where he lived and whether he was in the area. Rather than give up, they drew on something they already enjoyed, they regularly perform country music at senior living communities and other venues, so they began asking audiences whether anyone knew a Roger Reese. The trail led to Windsong, the senior living community where Reese was staying.Reese was setting up chairs for the concert when Fred Ambuehl approached him on 3 NovemberThe Washington Post reported that the two men had never met before early November, when Ambuehl and his wife approached Reese as he set up chairs for a concert by their country band. Reese regularly volunteers at community events. Both live in Bemidji, the small northern Minnesota town known for its giant statues of Paul Bunyan and Babe the Blue Ox.Lifetime Stories dates the reunion to 3 November, during a concert at the senior community. The couple said they bought his old vehicle and found something important while cleaning it: his wedding ring.The reunion stirred memories of Joan, and Vickie asked for nothing more than a hugThe ring belonged to a chapter of Reese's life that could never be repeated. Joan was no longer there to share the moment, but the band brought back memories of their years together, and he reportedly said it felt as though she was smiling at him.Asked what she wanted in return, Vickie requested only a hug. Reese then gave her the replacement ring he had bought at the pawnshop, as thanks for helping him recover something so important.The couple sold the replacement ring and planned a $500 donation to the Bemidji Veterans HomeFred and Vickie later sold the replacement ring to a jeweller, raising approximately $500, which they planned to donate to the Bemidji Veterans Home. They had every opportunity to keep the ring or leave it behind. Instead, they chose to trace its owner and kept asking until they found the right man.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic, while nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic, while nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in vitamin B12, pointing to a wider nutritional challenge that goes beyond iron deficiency, a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has found.The findings fill a key data gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which did not include anaemia estimates. Government had subsequently said these would be drawn from an independent ICMR survey based on venous blood samples.The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition's SAMPADA survey for 2023-25 found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years. NFHS-5 reported a prevalence of 57 per cent among women in the same age group. The figures, however, are not directly comparable because the surveys covered different groups of women and used different testing methods.State-wise estimates showed sharp regional disparities, with Andaman and Nicobar recording the highest prevalence at 81.2 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years.The burden was also high in other groups. Anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19 years. Among children, 41.8 per cent of those aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent of those aged 5-9 years were anaemic. The prevalence was 43.6 per cent among pregnant women and 58.1 per cent among lactating women. Among adult men aged 20-59 years, it stood at 22 per cent.B12 deficiency was more widespread among adolescents, affecting 65.4 per cent of girls and 66.1 per cent of boys. It was found in 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of adult men aged 20-59 years. The prevalence stood at 63.1 per cent among pregnant women and 51.8 per cent among lactating women.Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, despite anaemia affecting 46.3 per cent and 55.9 per cent of these groups, respectively. Iron deficiency itself remained common, affecting 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age, 29.6 per cent of pregnant women and 23 per cent of children aged 12-59 months, compared with 10 per cent for adolescent boys."Not all anaemia is caused by nutritional deficiencies such as iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, chronic kidney disease, tuberculosis and cancer can also cause anaemia. Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," said Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology, AIIMS."We have been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme to develop simple algorithms to identify such cases," Seth added.The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories, drawing data from over 81,000 households and analysing over 1.7 lakh blood samples.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress politician Rahul Gandhi said the security of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, was removed deliberately to get him killed, making a sensational charge years after the former PM was assassinated by a suicide bomber in Tamil Nadu.In a video interaction with his mother Sonia Gandhi and sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said, "Papa's security was removed so that he got killed. Papa's security removal was not an accident. It was done on purpose so that he got killed." "An atmosphere was created for him to get killed. It was obvious what was going on. I told papa and mom, and had an argument about it with my father," he said.Act passed by Rajiv government offered SPG cover only to PM, not former PMsRahul Tuesday posted a video featuring the family discussing Sonia Gandhi’s recently released book ‘Belonging’, in which his charge came just after his mother spoke about the lax security arrangements during Rajiv Gandhi’s visit to Bihar as leader of the opposition, where he faced stone pelting. Rahul had accompanied his father on his Bihar visit.Even though Rahul alleged there was an “intention” behind withdrawing his father’s security in 1988, the Special Protection Group Act, passed in 1988 by the then Rajiv government, restricted SPG cover strictly to the PM and not to former PMs. Thus, Rajiv lost the protection after being voted out in 1989. V P Singh replaced him as PM. When Rajiv was assassinated at a rally in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, the Chandra Shekhar government was in office.Following the assassination, the PV Narasimha Rao government amended the Act, extending protection to former PMs and their immediate family members for five years after leaving office. This brought Sonia, Rahul and Priyanka under its cover. It was further amended in 1994 to prolong the duration to 10 years.Rahul also said Sonia has not written about how she was treated by some people. He said she was “humiliated, abused” in politics, adding he may talk about it someday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Panchang Today is your steady, dependable guide for planning the day with precision, drawn from the living wisdom of the Hindu calendar. It tells you what the Moon is doing, which energies are supportive, and where you should slow down. In a busy Indian routine of office calls, school runs, shopping, and family duties, this daily map helps you stay connected to cultural roots and still make practical choices. Some days ask for courage, some for patience, and some for quiet resets. Today leans towards rebuilding after a pause. Below are the important Panchang details for November 25, 2026 for India:Date & Day DetailsDate & Day DetailsNovember 25, 2026 falls on Wednesday, and the lunar day is Krishan Paksh 1 (Pratipada(Ekam)) up to 16:50:21, after which Krishan Paksh 2 (Dvitiya) begins. Pratipada right after Amavasya is like the first thin line of light on a dark horizon. The Moon has just begun its Krishna Paksha journey, so emotions can feel fresh but also slightly raw. This is a day to start again, but not with loud announcements. Think of it as sweeping the floor before you bring new furniture home. It supports personal corrections, clearing clutter, repairing relationships with a simple message, and restarting healthy habits without showing off.The Nakshatra is Rohini till 20:36:22, moving later into Mrigasira. Rohini is guided by Prajapati Brahma, the force of creation and growth. That’s why Rohini energy often feels fertile, steady, and comfort-seeking. It favours activities that build value over time, like planning a monthly budget, buying necessities for the home, tending to plants, fine-tuning a project, or cooking with care. There’s also a soft pull towards beauty and pleasure, so keep an eye on indulgence. When the Nakshatra shifts to Mrigasira after 20:36:22, the mood becomes more curious and searching. Good for research, studying, and asking the right questions. Less good for impulsive decisions.The Moon remains in Taurus (Taurus 14.22) for the day, bringing a grounded, practical tone. Taurus Moon is slow and sure, like a bull that won’t budge once it decides. People may resist last-minute changes, so give others time and don’t push too hard. The Moon sign transition happens at 26/11/2026 07:10:59 into Gemini, which means today is still best used for stability and finishing tasks that need patience.Yoga is Shiva till 11:59:51, then Siddha begins. Shiva Yoga carries the spirit of inner cleansing and discipline. It’s supportive for simplifying life, cutting out wasteful spending, and speaking less but meaning more. After 11:59:51, Siddha Yoga brings a more accomplished, “things fall into place” feeling, especially for work that has been pending.Karan energies also set the rhythm. Balava runs till 06:37:42 and then Kaulava continues till 16:50:21, after which Taitila begins. Balava and Kaulava are generally supportive for routine action, communication, and steady progress. In short, this Wednesday asks for calm effort, clean intentions, and a little restraint.Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Your earliest sacred window is brahma_muhurta from 2026-11-25 04:36:05 to 2026-11-25 05:29:05. This time has a quiet, almost dew-covered purity. The mind is less noisy then, and prayers land deeper. Use it for japa, reading a few verses, or even sitting silently with your breath before the phone lights up with messages.pratah_sandhya runs from 2026-11-25 05:02:35 to 2026-11-25 06:22:05. It’s ideal for Surya arghya, lighting a lamp, or setting your intentions for the day. If you’ve been delaying exercise, start here. Even a short walk or a few rounds of stretching will feel more natural.Midday brings vijay_muhurta from 2026-11-25 13:32:05 to 2026-11-25 14:15:05. This is the “win your battle” pocket of time. Schedule an important meeting, send that assertive email, or push through a tough assignment then. Keep it clean and factual, no ego games.Evening is strong too. godhuli_muhurta appears from 2026-11-25 17:07:30 to 2026-11-25 17:34:00, and sayahana_sandhya stretches from 2026-11-25 17:07:30 to 2026-11-25 18:27:00. This twilight is perfect for aarti, gratitude prayers, and calming the home atmosphere. If the family’s been tense, even a simple shared tea and two kind sentences can shift the mood.amrit_kalam from 2026-11-25 17:46:19 to 2026-11-25 19:10:59 is especially supportive for meaningful steps, like paying an important bill mindfully, starting a savings habit, or beginning a serious study schedule.At night, nishita_muhurta arrives from 2026-11-25 23:18:30 to 2026-11-26 00:11:30. It’s suitable for deeper spiritual practices, quiet mantra, and honest self-reflection.A major window is sarvartha_siddhi_yoga from 2026-11-25 20:36:39 to 2026-11-26 06:22:49. It’s traditionally seen as supportive for many purposes, especially starting work that needs steady results.Choghadiya also guides practical scheduling. The day’s auspicious flow includes Laabh @ 06:22, Amrit @ 07:43, Shubh @ 10:24, and Laabh @ 15:47. At night, watch for Shubh @ 18:47, Amrit @ 20:27, and Laabh @ 27:04 when planning dinner, study, or family discussions.Inauspicious TimingsInauspicious TimingsRahu Kaal today is from 11:45 to 13:06. Rahu’s shadowy influence can cloud judgement and make small matters feel bigger than they are. During this period, avoid starting new ventures, signing contracts, or making big financial decisions. Keep your wallet closed today, especially for online shopping or a tempting “limited offer.” What should you do instead? Use the time for routine work, filing, cleaning your inbox, or quiet prayer. If you want a simple remedy, chant the Rahu mantra “Om Raam Rahave Namaha” a few times, or sit for ten minutes of steady breathing.Other sensitive windows also matter. y amaganda is from 2026-11-25 07:42:45 to 2026-11-25 09:03:26, a period best kept for normal activities rather than fresh starts. gulkai_kaal runs from 2026-11-25 10:24:06 to 2026-11-25 11:44:47, so keep expectations modest and avoid risky moves. There is dur_muhurtam from 2026-11-25 11:23:05 to 2026-11-25 12:06:05, overlapping the approach to Rahu Kaal, which is another reason to postpone important conversations with your boss or a heated family discussion.The Panchang also notes baana (Roga) from 2026-11-25 06:22:05 to 2026-11-25 17:45:05. This points to a day where health routines should not be ignored. Overeating, skipping water, or pushing through fatigue can backfire. Gentle discipline will save you time later.Yoga-based warnings appear too. samvartaka_yoga stretches from 2026-11-24 20:24:05 to 2026-11-25 06:21:05, so early morning may feel heavy if sleep was poor. Then aadal_yoga runs from 2026-11-25 06:22:05 to 2026-11-25 20:35:39, advising restraint in decisions and speech. Later, vidaal_yoga appears from 2026-11-25 20:36:39 to 2026-11-26 06:22:49, at the same time as sarvartha_siddhi_yoga. Mixed signals? Yes. It means results depend on intention and method. Choose clean actions, avoid shortcuts, and don’t initiate anything with anger or greed.Late night has varjyam from 2026-11-26 01:32:39 to 2026-11-26 02:57:13, best kept for rest.Choghadiya inauspicious pockets include Kaal @ 09:03, Rog @ 11:45, Udveg @ 13:06 in the day, and Udveg @ 17:08, Rog @ 23:45, Kaal @ 25:25, Udveg @ 28:43 at night. Use these for ordinary tasks, not for bold beginnings.Rahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal changes from place to place across India because it is calculated using local sunrise, and sunrise differs by longitude even within the same state. So the Rahu period you follow at home should match your local Panchang. The table below provides Rahu Kaal for major Indian cities, which helps travellers and families spread across regions stay aligned with the right timing.CityRahu KaalMumbai12:25 - 13:49Delhi (NCR)12:08 - 13:27Bengaluru12:07 - 13:32Hyderabad12:03 - 13:27Chennai11:56 - 13:22Ahmedabad12:26 - 13:48Pune12:21 - 13:45Kolkata11:23 - 12:45Jaipur12:14 - 13:34Kochi12:12 - 13:39Lucknow11:53 - 13:13Indore12:13 - 13:35Guwahati11:10 - 12:30Chandigarh12:09 - 13:27Surat12:25 - 13:48Visakhapatnam11:44 - 13:08Nagpur12:00 - 13:23Coimbatore12:09 - 13:36Varanasi11:45 - 13:06Bhubaneswar11:33 - 12:56Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise is at 06:22:20, and sunset follows at 17:08:20. These times shape the day’s tempo in a very real way. Sunrise is the day’s first spiritual bell, reminding you to begin clean, speak less sharply, and keep your promises small but solid. If you can’t do a full prayer routine, even lighting a lamp near sunrise brings focus.Sunset at 17:08:20 marks the shift from outer effort to inner settling. It’s the natural moment to slow the pace, return calls with patience, and drop the habit of carrying office stress into the living room. Twilight practices done near this transition often feel soothing because the mind is already turning inward.Moonrise is at 05:36:09 PM, and moonset is at 08:15:17 AM, Nov 26. With the Moon in Taurus and Rohini influence for most of the day, the evening can feel emotionally full, even if the sky looks calm. You may crave comfort food, familiar music, or a quiet talk with someone you trust. Choose comfort that heals, not comfort that drains. Before sleep, keep the phone away for a bit and let the mind settle like silt in a pond. The next morning’s moonset reminds you that feelings also pass. Don’t cling. Observe, learn, and move on.Vrat/Festival Information & RecommendationsVrat/Festival Information & RecommendationsNo major Vrat or festival is observed today. The Hindu month is Kartika in the amanta tradition and Margashirsha in the purnimanta tradition, and that blend carries a gentle shift in mood. Kartika’s lingering spiritual warmth encourages simplicity, devotion, and cleanliness of habits. Margashirsha brings a more focused, purposeful flavour, like the air after the first winter breeze when you suddenly want to get life in order.So what should you do with this day? Keep it steady and honest. With Krishan Paksh 1 (Pratipada(Ekam)) till 16:50:21, treat the first half like a reset button. Clear pending messages. Fix small household issues you’ve been ignoring. Pay attention to food and sleep because baana (Roga) from 2026-11-25 06:22:05 to 2026-11-25 17:45:05 suggests your body will protest if you act careless.For relationships, Rohini in Taurus asks for warmth but not drama. Speak softly, even if you feel stubborn. A small gesture works better than a long lecture. If you need to apologise, do it simply, no “but you also…” attached.At work, this is a day to show reliability. Finish what you started. Keep your boss updated with one clear message instead of multiple scattered ones. Use vijay_muhurta from 2026-11-25 13:32:05 to 2026-11-25 14:15:05 to push a plan forward, but avoid big sign-offs during Rahu Kaal from 11:45 to 13:06.For spiritual practice, use brahma_muhurta from 2026-11-25 04:36:05 to 2026-11-25 05:29:05 if you can, and lean into evening prayer during sayahana_sandhya from 2026-11-25 17:07:30 to 2026-11-25 18:27:00. The night window sarvartha_siddhi_yoga from 2026-11-25 20:36:39 to 2026-11-26 06:22:49 can be powerful if your intention is clean, but vidaal_yoga runs at the same time, so avoid shortcuts, gossip, and late-night spending.End the day like you’d close a door gently, not with a bang. Eat light, drink enough water, and set tomorrow’s clothes and to-do list before sleep. articles.body: General:The Moon remains in Taurus in your fifth house all day, drawing attention to learning, enjoyment and personal expectations. You may feel enthusiastic about a plan yet find your concentration wandering. Productive work is still possible if you choose a clear aim. Leave some room for pleasure without making the day depend on praise or a particular result. If a gathering is possible, decide what you can comfortably attend rather than trying to fit in every invitation.Love and Relationship:An interest you share can make conversation easier than a discussion about what the relationship ought to be. If children or younger people need your attention, encourage effort without predicting an outcome for them. The retrograde Rahu-Ketu axis connects Rahu in Aquarius in your second house with Ketu in Leo in your eighth house. This asks for care with family speech and private concerns. Say what you mean without using money or past sacrifices to strengthen your argument.Education and Career:Your ruler Saturn is retrograde in Pisces in your third house, a constructive longer-term position for sustained effort, communication and practical skills. Progress may come through practising what feels repetitive. Students can benefit from active recall rather than reading the same page without testing understanding. Mercury and Venus are in Libra in your tenth house, with Venus in its own sign. A clear presentation and courteous professional manner can help your work receive a fair hearing, without guaranteeing recognition.Money and Finance:Jupiter in Leo in your eighth house calls for scrutiny of shared finances, obligations and uncertain commitments. Do not treat an expected reimbursement, settlement or contribution as money already available. Mars is also in Leo in your eighth house, making it useful to pause before pressing ahead with a complicated financial task. Review who owes what and when. If business expansion involves travel, assess the full cost and likely purpose before paying a deposit.Health and Well-being:Enjoyment and physical activity can fit into the day, but neither needs to become a performance. If you play sport, give preparation and technique the same attention as the result. Mental distraction may be a reason to simplify your schedule, not abandon it. A short recreational break can refresh you more than switching repeatedly between work and messages. articles.title: At 29, Pune's Priya Bodke chose farming over office work near Hinjawadi's IT hub; she now helps organic farmers sell directly to customers through an app offering around 123 products, from vegetables to ghee
articles.summary: Just 1.5 kilometres from Pune's Hinjawadi IT Park, where thousands of professionals work in technology companies, Priya Bodke chose a different career.
articles.body: Just 1.5 kilometres from Pune's Hinjawadi IT Park, where thousands of professionals work in technology companies, Priya Bodke chose a different career. After completing Class 12, she decided to pursue agriculture rather than look for an office job. Now 29, she handles the direct marketing of organic produce for Abhinav Farmers Club, helping farmers connect with customers through a digital platform that lists around 123 products.As reported by The Indian Express, Priya grew up in Maan village in a family that has been involved in farming for four generations. Her father has practised organic farming for 35 years. Watching him work, she came to believe that agriculture could provide a viable livelihood if it was managed as a business.She went on to complete a Bachelor of Science degree in Horticulture in Pune. Today, she works with Abhinav Farmers Club, an organic farming collective based in Mulshi taluka, Pune district.Choosing farming over an office jobThe choice was not the usual one in an area known for its IT companies. Bodke told The Indian Express that many of her neighbours work in Hinjawadi's technology firms, earning salaries but following fixed office hours. She prefers the flexibility of organising her own schedule around farm work and marketing.The farm also receives around 50 to 60 visitors every day. Bodke sets aside specific hours to attend to them and uses the remaining time for her work and lectures. She believes that many young people turn away from agriculture because their parents did not earn enough from farming. In her view, the sector needs to be approached as a business, with attention to production, marketing and customer needs.An app that connects farmers with customersBodke's work at Abhinav Farmers Club focuses on getting the produce of its member farmers to consumers directly. Farmers grow the products, which are then collected, sorted and graded at a pack house before being delivered to customers who place orders through the club's app.According to The Indian Express, the app's catalogue features around 123 products, including vegetables, fruits, grains, cooking oil and ghee. The collective sells through its own platform rather than listing its products on other online marketplaces.The digital ordering system has evolved over time. Initially, the club used a basic app developed by students at IIT Bombay for two to three years. It has since developed its own app and website.Bodke also helped train young women from farming families in app development and web design. They now work on maintaining both platforms. She believes that involving people familiar with agriculture helps ensure that the technology addresses the actual needs of farmers.According to the club's official website, its model is integrated organic farming and direct marketing. The collective works with farmers to supply vegetables, fruits, grains, pulses, A2 milk and dairy products to households across Maharashtra.A farmer-led model of direct marketingAbhinav Farmers Club's approach has also been documented in government reports. A case study in the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare's Sector Report: Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Fisheries describes how the group combines organic cultivation with direct marketing. It explains that farmers coordinate production and that women’s self-help groups help with grading, packaging and doorstep delivery.The club began in 2004 and has expanded its network across several states. Its members supply produce directly to households, reducing dependence on intermediaries.For Bodke, the work involves more than listing products on an app. She coordinates the movement of produce from member farmers to customers, while also helping young women from farming families learn skills to maintain the digital platform. Her workplace is close to one of Pune's largest IT hubs, but her career is built around a different kind of business: helping farmers reach the people who buy their food.You use AI every day.
